SRDatalog - Nim Wrapper for SRDatalog Runtime

This module provides the main entry point for using SRDatalog from Nim. SRDatalog (Super Reconfigurable Datalog) is a high-performance Datalog engine framework with support for generalized semirings, enabling provenance tracking, probabilistic reasoning, and other advanced Datalog features. The "SR" prefix emphasizes the framework's super reconfigurable architecture, enabling users to build custom Datalog engines by swapping data structure backends, runtime mechanisms, and optimization strategies.

Overview

SRDatalog combines:

  • Nim's expressive syntax: Write Datalog programs using a clean DSL
  • C++ runtime performance: Generated code uses optimized C++ data structures
  • Generalized semirings: Support for Boolean, probabilistic, and custom semirings
  • Column-oriented storage: Efficient SoA (Structure of Arrays) layout
  • HashTrie indexing: Fast multi-level indexes for efficient joins

Quick Start

See the example programs in src/example/ for complete working examples:

  • triangle.nim: Non-recursive multi-way join query
  • tc.nim: Recursive transitive closure using fixpoint rules

Basic usage:

import srdatalog/lang

srdatalog_prelude()

# Define database schema (reusable across modules/macros)
schema MyDB:
  Edge: Relation[int, int]
  Path: Relation[int, int]

datalog_db(MyDB, MyDBCode())

# Define base case (non-recursive)
none_recursive_rule BaseCase, MyDBCode():
  [{(Path x y)} <-- {(Edge x y)}] {. name: Base order: [x, y] .}

# Define recursive case (fixpoint)
fixpoint_rule TransitiveClosure, MyDBCode():
  [{(Path x z)} <-- {(Path x y) (Edge y z)}] {. name: TC order: [y, x, z] .}

# Create database with memory arenas
var arena_full = newArena()
var arena_delta = newArena()
var arena_newt = newArena()
{.emit: "SemiNaiveDatabase<MyDB> db(&`arena_full`, &`arena_delta`, &`arena_newt`);".}

# Add facts
edb db:
  (Edge ($"BooleanSR::one()") ($"1") ($"2"))
  (Edge ($"BooleanSR::one()") ($"2") ($"3"))

Architecture

The Nim wrapper uses compile-time code generation:

  1. Macro Expansion: Nim macros parse Datalog syntax
  2. AST Generation: Creates an abstract syntax tree
  3. C++ Code Generation: Emits optimized C++ code using {.emit.}
  4. Runtime Execution: C++ runtime executes the generated code

This hybrid approach gives you:

  • Type safety at compile time (Nim)
  • Runtime performance (C++)
  • Clean, declarative syntax (Datalog DSL)

Why Nim as a Meta Language?

Nim serves as a powerful meta language for building Datalog compilers, offering several key advantages:

AST Manipulation and Optimization: Datalog compiler users can leverage Nim's macro system to easily manipulate the AST of queries. This enables sophisticated optimizations, query rewriting, and even join planning at compile time. The macro system provides a clean, high-level interface for transforming Datalog programs before code generation.

Configurable Backend Architecture: The framework is designed for maximum configurability and reusability. Users can reset the data structure backend by reloading the relations API and executor function, allowing support for different data structures and runtime mechanisms. This makes SRDatalog not just a Datalog engine, but a framework for building your own Datalog engines tailored to specific use cases.

C++ Integration: Nim can be considered as an external macro system for C++. By using Nim's {.emit.} blocks and C++ backend, the framework generates optimized C++ code while providing a more ergonomic metaprogramming environment than raw C++ template metaprogramming. This approach combines the expressiveness of Nim's macros with the performance and ecosystem of C++.

Framework Reusability: The combination of Nim's metaprogramming capabilities and the modular design of the C++ runtime creates a highly reusable framework. Developers can extend the system by:

  • Writing custom AST transformations using Nim macros
  • Implementing new data structure backends by providing alternative relation APIs
  • Creating specialized executors for different runtime environments (e.g., distributed, GPU-accelerated)
  • Customizing optimization passes and query planning strategies

This architecture makes SRDatalog an ideal foundation for research and production Datalog systems that need fine-grained control over compilation and execution.

Future Meta Language Support: While Nim is currently the primary meta language, the framework is designed to support additional meta languages in the future. In particular, Racket with C JIT compile library setup is planned as an alternative meta language option, providing another powerful metaprogramming environment for Datalog compiler development.
